title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
statement: Points are given as [x, y] on the plane. The cost of connecting two points is the Manhattan distance. Return the minimum cost to connect every point, which is the weight of a minimum spanning tree.
hints: The complete graph is implicit. You do not need to store every edge for Prim.
Prim grows one component. The next edge is the cheapest edge from the component to an outside point.
Manhattan distance is abs(x1 - x2) + abs(y1 - y2).

approaches.name: Kruskal on all pairs
approaches.explanation: Sort every edge and union until one component remains.

approaches.name: Prim
approaches.explanation: Dense Prim scans all outside points each step and is optimal for a complete graph.

editorial: Start from point 0. Keep the cheapest known connection from the tree to every outside point. Add the outside point with the smallest connection, then update the other outside points with the distance to the newly added point. The sum of the chosen connections is the MST cost. A single point costs 0.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def min_cost_connect_points(points: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    n = len(points)
    in_tree = [False] * n
    best = [10**18] * n
    best[0] = 0
    total = 0
    for _ in range(n):
        u = min((best[i], i) for i in range(n) if not in_tree[i])[1]
        in_tree[u] = True
        total += best[u]
        x, y = points[u]
        for v in range(n):
            if not in_tree[v]:
                dist = abs(points[v][0] - x) + abs(points[v][1] - y)
                best[v] = min(best[v], dist)
    return total
